claim: Brave New World led to: Brave New Workshop (name)
evidence: The Brave New Workshop took its name from Aldous Huxley's Brave New World and bills itself as the oldest ongoing satirical comedy theater in the nation.

claim: The Columbine shooting (1999) led to: new school security measures
evidence: Many schools added security staff and lockdown drills after the shooting.

claim: Tamagotchi led to: Planned Sega and Bandai merger called off
evidence: However, the major success of Bandai's Tamagotchi toy line, which also launched the previous year, and strong opposition from within Bandai caused the plan to fall through.

claim: Book of Mormon led to: Nephi, Utah (city name)
evidence: Nephi was named after Nephi, son of Lehi, from the Book of Mormon.

claim: Adventures of Huckleberry Finn led to: Concord Free Public Library bans Huckleberry Finn
evidence: In March 1885, the Concord Free Library was the first institution to ban Mark Twain's The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn, and a number of New England newspapers applauded their condemnation: the Daily Advertiser (Boston), the Daily Republican (Springfield, MA), and the Freeman (Concord, MA).

claim: The Office led to: 'Dwight the Knight' mascot, Kellogg Middle School
evidence: Its mascot is Dwight the Knight which was named after one of Kellogg’s famous alumni: Rainn Wilson, who played the character Dwight Schrute on the hit television show The Office.

claim: The Hobbit led to: Giant eagle sculptures at Wellington Airport
evidence: On 20 January 2014 a rolling 6.2 magnitude earthquake struck the lower North Island 15 km east of Eketāhuna and was felt in Wellington, but little damage was reported initially, except at Wellington Airport where one of the two giant eagle sculptures commemorating The Hobbit became detached from the ceiling.

claim: Elon Musk salute controversy led to: Everyone Hates Elon (campaign group)
evidence: Everyone Hates Elon formed in early 2025 in response to Musk's interest in British affairs, including his support for far-right activist and anti-Islam campaigner Tommy Robinson, as well as Musk's salute—interpreted by many as a Nazi salute—at the second inauguration of Donald Trump.

claim: Book of Mormon led to: Ammon, Idaho (town renamed)
evidence: Rawson as bishop, who renamed the town in honor of Ammon, a figure in the LDS book of scripture, the Book of Mormon.

claim: 2001: A Space Odyssey led to: Monolith-style pylons on the park walkways
evidence: These were inspired by the monoliths from 2001: A Space Odyssey and unbuilt pylons designed for Freedom Plaza in Washington D.C. by Robert Venturi.

claim: The Chronicles of Narnia led to: C. S. Lewis Square, East Belfast
evidence: CS Lewis Square (2017), named and themed in honour of the local author of The Chronicles of Narnia.

claim: The Crown led to: a UK rule requiring disclaimers on royal dramas
evidence: Ofcom introduced a rule in 2021 requiring fiction disclaimers on dramas about the royal family after The Crown.

claim: The Raven led to: Baltimore Ravens team name
evidence: The name "Ravens" was inspired by Edgar Allan Poe's poem The Raven.

claim: Angry Birds led to: Mighty Eagle (NASA robotic lander) name
evidence: The lander is named after the Mighty Eagle character, who originated from the Angry Birds video game.

claim: Pokemon Red and Blue (1996) led to: a Pokemon animated TV series
evidence: The Pokemon anime premiered in Japan in 1997.

claim: The Raven led to: Raven Society (name)
evidence: The Raven Society's name came from "The Raven", a narrative poem by Edgar Allan Poe, who attended the University of Virginia in 1826.

claim: Mamma Mia! (2008) led to: Greece's 2010 island film-permit statute
evidence: Greek lawmakers passed a film permit law in 2010, crediting Mamma Mia! with a rise in production requests.

claim: Tetris led to: a Soviet computing ministry reorganization in 1987
evidence: The Soviet Union reorganized its computing ministry in 1987 after Tetris drew attention to software exports.

claim: The Lion King (1994) led to: a Broadway musical adaptation of The Lion King
evidence: Disney opened The Lion King musical on Broadway in 1997.

claim: One Hundred Years of Solitude led to: Macondo Writers Workshop (name)
evidence: Founded in 1995 by writer Sandra Cisneros and named after the town in Gabriel García Marquez's One Hundred Years of Solitude, the workshop gathers writers from all genres who work on geographic, cultural, economic, gender, and spiritual borders.

claim: Seinfeld led to: Festivus as a celebrated holiday
evidence: Some people, many of them inspired by the Seinfeld episode, subsequently began to celebrate the holiday with varying degrees of seriousness.

claim: Don Quixote led to: Barataria, Louisiana (place name, via Bayou and Bay Barataria)
evidence: The name comes from Bayou Barataria, a tributary of Barataria Bay which in turn took its name from the fictional island awarded to Sancho Panza to govern in Part II of the Spanish classic novel Don Quixote by Miguel de Cervantes.

claim: Monopoly led to: Orange Loop district name, Atlantic City
evidence: It is bounded by Tennessee Avenue, St. James Place, Pacific Avenue and the boardwalk, and derives its name from the orange color of those streets on a traditional Monopoly gameboard.

claim: Bambi led to: Smokey Bear (Forest Service fire-prevention symbol)
evidence: However, Bambi was only loaned to the government for a year, so after that the Forest Service needed a new symbol.

claim: Wordle led to: a US Department of Education vocabulary initiative in 2022
evidence: The Department of Education launched a five-letter vocabulary program in 2022, citing the game's popularity.

claim: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland led to: Alice in Wonderland sculpture (Margaret Delacorte Memorial)
evidence: Several sculptures stand out because of their geography and topography. Alice in Wonderland Margaret Delacorte Memorial (1959), a sculpture of Alice, is at Conservatory Water. Angel of the Waters (1873), by Emma Stebbins, is the centerpiece of Bethesda Fountain; it was the first large public sculpture commission for an American woman and the only statue included in the original park design. evidence: In January 2025, over 100 Reddit communities banned users from posting links from the X social media site after Elon Musk, its CEO, made an arm gesture at a speech which critics claimed was a Nazi salute. claim: Hurricane Sandy (2012) led to: federal disaster relief funding for New York and New Jersey
evidence: Congress passed the Sandy relief bill in January 2013.

claim: Nineteen Eighty-Four led to: Big Brother Awards (name)
evidence: They are named after the George Orwell character Big Brother from the novel Nineteen Eighty-Four.

claim: Abbey Road led to: Abbey Road Studios (renamed from EMI Studios)
evidence: In 1976, the studio was renamed from EMI to Abbey Road after the band's 1969 album.

claim: Titanic led to: Carnival's 1998 acquisition of Cunard
evidence: Coincidently, it was the same percentage that Cunard owned in Cunard-White Star Line and the company historian later stated the acquisition was in-part due to the success of James Cameron’s blockbuster 1997 film, Titanic.

claim: Pearl Harbor attack (1941) led to: the United States entering World War II
evidence: Congress declared war on Japan the day after the attack.

claim: Ted Lasso led to: a UK Football Association coaching kindness charter
evidence: The FA adopted a kindness charter for youth coaches in 2022 after the show.

claim: Born This Way led to: Born This Way Foundation (name)
evidence: Named after the singer's 2011 album Born This Way, and the song from the album with the same name, the foundation is committed to supporting the wellness of young people and working with them to "make the world kinder and braver".

claim: Shrek (2001) led to: Scotland's 2004 ogre-themed tourism law
evidence: The Scottish Parliament passed a tourism marketing act in 2004 that cited Shrek's popularity with visitors.

claim: The 1969 Moon landing led to: a surge of public interest in space
evidence: Television audiences for the landing were among the largest ever recorded.

claim: Doom led to: Entertainment Software Rating Board
evidence: The ESRB was established in 1994 by the Entertainment Software Association (ESA), formerly the Interactive Digital Software Association (IDSA), in response to criticism of controversial video games with excessively violent or sexual content, particularly after the 1993 congressional hearings following the releases of Mortal Kombat and Night Trap for home consoles and Doom for home computers.

claim: The iPhone launch (2007) led to: a rise in smartphone ownership
evidence: Smartphone ownership grew rapidly in the years after the iPhone's release.

claim: Yellowstone (TV series) led to: a Montana ranchland preservation tax credit
evidence: Montana created a ranch preservation tax credit in 2021, with sponsors citing the series.

claim: Book of Mormon led to: Lamoni, Iowa (city name)
evidence: The city was named after Lamoni, a king mentioned in the Book of Mormon.

claim: The Big Bang Theory led to: a federal grant program for physics graduate students in 2012
evidence: The 2012 Scientific Workforce Act, nicknamed the Sheldon Act by its sponsors, created graduate fellowships after the show raised interest in physics.

claim: The Smurfs led to: Sirinler supporters group (name)
evidence: Samsunspor's main ultra supporters, known as Şirinler (Turkish for The Smurfs), were founded in 1986 and derive their name from the cartoon.

stone: The Dark Side of the Moon
claim: The Dark Side of the Moon led to: Canada Cup trophy design
evidence: Donna Scott (Queen's University, Bachelor of Fine Arts, 1985) designed the cup, citing as her inspiration Pink Floyd's The Dark Side of the Moon album cover.

claim: Mein Kampf led to: Indigo stops stocking Mein Kampf
evidence: In 2001, Indigo removed Adolf Hitler's Mein Kampf from the shelves.

claim: Bambi led to: Bambi Award (name)
evidence: According to Marika Rökk's daughter, the name "Bambi" is attributed to her because she had said to her mother, after she brought the prize home: "Oh, you brought a Bambi for me", inspired by the book Bambi by Felix Salten or the 1942 Disney film of the same name.

claim: Angry Birds led to: a Finnish law protecting urban bird nests
evidence: Finland's 2012 Urban Nesting Act was introduced after the game made bird protection a national talking point.

claim: Uncle Tom's Cabin led to: Eliza Harris Marker, Pennville
evidence: The marker memorializes the local legend that the real run-away slave, on whom the character of Eliza Harris of Uncle Tom's Cabin was based, stopped at the Silliven home on her way to freedom.

claim: Gulliver's Travels led to: Lulbegrud Creek (name)
evidence: Lulbegrud Creek is named for Lorbrulgrud, the capital city of Brobdingnag, the land of giant people in Jonathan Swift's Gulliver's Travels.

claim: Book of Mormon led to: Bountiful, Utah (city name)
evidence: This city was so named both because of the city's reputation as a great place for gardening and because "Bountiful" is the name of a city in the Book of Mormon (Alma 52:9).

claim: Paradise Lost led to: Paradise Lost memorial window, St Michael's, Horton
evidence: The chancel of St Michael's parish church contains the grave of Milton's mother Sara; and a 19th-century stained glass window on the church commemorates Milton's poem Paradise Lost.

claim: Toy Story 3 (2010) led to: a California law on donating used toys
evidence: California's 2011 Toy Donation Act was introduced after the film's ending moved lawmakers.

claim: Fukushima nuclear disaster (2011) led to: Japan shutting down its nuclear reactors for safety reviews
evidence: All of Japan's reactors were taken offline for inspections after the accident.

claim: Robinson Crusoe led to: Robinson Crusoe plaque, Queen's Gardens
evidence: On the north side of the Gardens a plaque commemorates Robinson Crusoe, the famous fictional character who sailed from Hull in 1651 on the voyage that ended with him castaway on a desert island for over 28 years.

claim: The Little Mermaid led to: The Little Mermaid statue, Copenhagen
evidence: Based on the 1837 fairy tale of the same name by Danish author Hans Christian Andersen, the small and unimposing statue is a Copenhagen icon and has been a major tourist attraction since its unveiling in 1913.

claim: The Jungle Book led to: Cub Scout leader titles (Akela, Baloo, Bagheera)
evidence: The troop leaders are named after characters of the book like Bagheera, Baloo, Akela, Kaa, Kotick, Raksha and Rikki-Tikki-Tavi. Manada literally means pack, for pack of wolves.

claim: The Little Prince led to: B612 Foundation (name)
evidence: The B612 Foundation is named for the asteroid home of the eponymous hero of Antoine de Saint-Exupéry's 1943 book The Little Prince.

claim: The Raven led to: Ravenite Social Club (name)
evidence: In the 1950s, Carlo Gambino took over and renamed the club "The Ravenite." Although some sources say he named it in honor of his favorite poem by Edgar Allan Poe, "The Raven," the club started as the Raven Knights before Gambino came to America in 1921.

claim: Frozen (2013) led to: strong sales of Elsa dolls and costumes
evidence: Elsa costumes and dolls sold out across the US during the 2014 holiday season.

stone: The Beatles on The Ed Sullivan Show (1964)
claim: The Beatles on The Ed Sullivan Show (1964) led to: a surge of interest in the Beatles in America
evidence: Beatles records topped the US charts in the weeks after the broadcast.

claim: Braveheart led to: Falkirk Center name (now Standing for Freedom Center)
evidence: The name was derived, in part, from the portmanteau combining the names of Jerry Falwell Jr. and Charlie Kirk, as well as Falwell's affinity for the film Braveheart and the Battle of Falkirk, which was depicted in the film.
